starting_principles: Macroscopic resistance definition for a uniform conductor: $R = \rho \frac{l}{A}$
Volumetric conservation of an incompressible solid: $V = A \cdot l = \text{constant}$
Cross-sectional area of a uniform circular cylinder of radius $r$: $A = \pi r^2$
assumptions: Zero mass loss during drawing, stretching, or melting and recasting
Material density $\rho_m$ is constant, ensuring volume invariance ($V_1 = V_2 = V$)
Resistivity $\rho$ remains constant (isothermal condition and microstructural integrity)
Uniform circular cylindrical shape is maintained throughout the conductor length

ordered_steps.description: State the macroscopic resistance formula for a uniform cylindrical conductor.
ordered_steps.operation: Express electrical resistance in terms of intrinsic resistivity $\rho$, conductor length $l$, and cross-sectional area $A$

ordered_steps.description: Formulate the volumetric conservation constraint during recasting or stretching.
ordered_steps.operation: Enforce $V_1 = V_2 = V = \text{constant}$ under mass and density conservation
assumptions_applied: Incompressible material with zero mass loss

ordered_steps.description: Express electrical resistance as an explicit function of length $l$ under volume conservation.
Express electrical resistance as an explicit function of cross-sectional area $A$ under volume conservation.
Substitute circular cylindrical geometry in terms of radius $r$ and diameter $d$.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $A = \pi r^2$ and $A = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}$ into the volume-dependent resistance relation

ordered_steps.description: Formulate the scaling ratio connecting initial and final resistances upon wire deformation.
ordered_steps.operation: Divide $R_2$ by $R_1$ to eliminate common physical constants $\rho$ and $V$
assumptions_applied: Identical material resistivity $\rho$ before and after recasting

applicability_conditions: Volume conservation holds strictly ($V = A l = \text{constant}$)
Resistivity $\rho$ is invariant during the geometric transformation
Cross-sectional shape remains uniform along the length of the conductor
